  p.brand,
  ROUND(SUM(s.net_amount), 2) AS net_revenue
FROM contoso_served.v_contoso5_sales_line AS s

sections.title: What it says its rows are

body.value: How much money each of the eleven brands Contoso sells under actually took from customers after discount, over all ten years of sales on record — order dates 2016-05-18 to 2025-12-31 — counting the walk-in shops and the web shop together, one row per brand, biggest earner first, in USD. The eleven figures add to 218,814,471.66 over 223,974 sales lines, which is every sale in the warehouse to the cent, so this is a complete split of the business rather than a sample or a top-N. WHAT I DID NOT TAKE OUT: this is after discount and after nothing else — no returns, refunds, tax or shipping is subtracted, because the bundle holds no such figure; if your books mean something narrower by "net", this is not that figure. WHAT I DID NOT SPLIT OUT: the web shop is folded into each brand's number, not shown separately, and it is 86,790,054.13 of the total — so a brand's figure here is its shop sales and its online sales combined. WHAT I DID NOT USE: delivery dates, which run six days further into 2026, and list prices, which are what products are catalogued at rather than what they sold for. One caution on reading it: volume does not track money here. Contoso's products appear on 59,896 lines and take less than Adventure Works' 22,362, and Southridge Video is third by lines but seventh by revenue — cheap-goods brands, not small ones.

  ROUND(SUM(s.net_amount), 2) AS net_revenue
